elements.element: New York law governs the Agreement.
elements.evidence: Section 10.5 retained unchanged: "This Agreement shall be governed and construed and enforced in accordance with the laws of the State of New York ... without giving effect to the principles of conflict of laws."

elements.element: State and federal courts in New York County have exclusive jurisdiction over the merits, subject only to temporary injunctive relief elsewhere.
elements.evidence: Added sentence: "The state and federal courts located in New York County, New York shall have exclusive jurisdiction over the merits of any dispute arising out of or relating to this Agreement, provided that either Party may seek temporary injunctive relief in any other court of competent jurisdiction." The only carve-out is customary temporary injunctive relief, which preserves the exclusive merits forum.

elements.element: The governing law is Delaware, California, or England and Wales.
elements.evidence: The clause selects New York law, not Delaware, California, or England and Wales. Not required, since the preferred level is satisfied.

elements.element: The dispute forum is the corresponding Delaware or California courts, or the courts of London for England and Wales law.
elements.evidence: Forum is New York County courts, not Delaware/California courts or the courts of London. Not required, since the preferred level is satisfied.

reasons: Preferred level is complete: existing New York governing law is retained verbatim and a single inserted sentence supplies the missing exclusive New York County forum with only a temporary-injunctive-relief carve-out.

Minimal: the redline adds one concise sentence to fill an absent forum provision, deletes nothing, and adds no survival tails, fee-shifting, service-of-process, jury-waiver, or other extras outside the checklist.

Intent preserved: the conflict-of-laws and 'contracts made and to be performed exclusively in that State' language survives intact; no undefined terms, dangling cross-references, or contradictory retained sentences are created (no arbitration or other venue clause exists to conflict).
Fallback elements are unmet only because a different accepted jurisdiction was chosen; position-completeness is satisfied at the preferred level.
